title: Private Log Export Integration Matrix (VPC + On‑prem/Air‑gapped) — Minimum Pack v1
content:
Last reviewed: 2025-08-12 (notes folded in from Splunk HEC 401 ticket + air-gap packaging feedback)

Purpose
- Provide a single view of which log export targets are supported for Redwood Private “observability minimum pack” (VPC + on‑prem/air‑gapped).
- Clarify: support level (validated vs documented), auth modes, and what the customer must provide (endpoints, CA bundles, network policy/egress, index naming, etc.).

Scope / assumptions
- Collector: Vector daemonset (default in minimum pack). Customers can replace the collector, but Redwood supportability applies only to the shipped config templates.
- Log types included:
  - Control plane operational logs (API gateway, policy/routing, auth integration points)
  - Data plane operational logs (serving runtime pods)
  - Installer/upgrade controller logs
- Excludes: audit logs (handled separately; see Security doc). Audit log export may share the same sink but has separate retention/access requirements.
- Redaction: request/response payloads are NOT logged by default; structured fields are limited to safe identifiers (e.g., request_id, route, model, status) with tenant_id hashed where applicable.

Support level definitions (used in matrix)
- VALIDATED: tested in reference environments (VPC + on‑prem-like), included in smoke tests, Support runbook exists.
- DOCUMENTED: config example provided; not part of automated validation; best‑effort troubleshooting.
- NOT IN V1: explicitly out of minimum pack v1; may be revisited.

Customer prerequisites (common)
- Provide sink endpoint(s) and DNS resolution inside the cluster (or via proxy).
- Provide TLS material as Kubernetes secrets:
  - CA bundle for custom/internal CAs
  - Optional client cert/key for mTLS targets
- Ensure NetworkPolicies and firewall rules allow egress from the collector namespace to the sink.
- Confirm retention/ILM policies are owned by the customer sink (Redwood does not manage retention in customer SIEM/ELK).
- If air‑gapped: sink is reachable on internal network; no outbound internet assumed; images/artifacts mirrored.

Configuration knobs shipped in Helm values (names approximate; see Helm PR wiring)
- logging.export.enabled (bool)
- logging.export.target (splunk_hec | elasticsearch | loki | otlp_http)
- logging.export.endpoint (url)
- logging.export.tls.caSecret / certSecret (secret names)
- logging.export.auth.* (tokenSecret | username/password secret | headers)
- logging.export.buffer.* (memory/disk buffer sizes, retries)

Integration matrix

| Export Target | VPC (connected) | On‑prem (connected) | On‑prem (air‑gapped) | Transport / Protocol | Auth modes supported (v1) | Customer prerequisites / gotchas | Support level | Notes / references |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| Splunk (HEC) | Yes | Yes | Yes* | HTTPS (HEC events endpoint) | HEC token (header), TLS, optional proxy | - Splunk HEC enabled + token created
- Customer provides endpoint + token secret
- If using Splunk w/ internal CA: provide CA bundle
- Some clusters require explicit allowlist for egress 443
- Common failure: HEC 401 due to token scope / wrong endpoint path (/services/collector/event vs raw) | VALIDATED | Linear ENG-19150; Jira SUP-49277 (HEC 401); ensure time sync/NTP (Splunk indexing pain) |
| Elasticsearch / OpenSearch | Yes | Yes | Yes* | HTTPS (bulk indexing) | Basic auth; API key header (documented); TLS; (SigV4 NOT in v1) | - Customer provides index template + ILM/retention
- Confirm mapping for structured fields (avoid dynamic mapping explosions)
- Use dedicated index prefix (e.g., redwood-private-logs-*)
- Provide CA bundle for internal clusters
- Watch shard count + ingestion limits (backpressure will drop if buffers exceed limits) | VALIDATED (Basic auth) / DOCUMENTED (API key) | Linear ENG-19151; recommended to pin index name + daily rollover |
| Grafana Loki | Yes | Yes | Yes* | HTTPS (Loki push API) | Basic auth; bearer token header; TLS; optional tenant header | - Loki endpoint reachable from cluster
- Multi-tenant Loki: customer must specify tenant header/value
- If using gateway (nginx): confirm max body size for batch payloads
- Retention configured in Loki, not in Redwood | DOCUMENTED | Supported for customers already running Loki; not in automated smoke tests yet |
| OTLP HTTP (logs) to Collector/Backend (e.g., OpenTelemetry Collector, Datadog/others via OTel gateway) | Yes | Yes | Conditional** | HTTP(S) OTLP logs | Static headers (API key), bearer token header, TLS | - Customer provides OTLP endpoint (often an in-cluster OTel Collector)
- Field mapping varies across vendors; customer owns final parsing
- Expect limited troubleshooting (headers/certs/connectivity only)
- Air‑gapped depends on whether vendor backend is reachable internally (usually requires in-cluster gateway) | DOCUMENTED | Debated in eng-infra thread; included as “escape hatch” for integrations |
| Syslog (TCP/UDP) | No | No | No | Syslog | N/A | Out of scope for v1 (security + parsing + reliability concerns) | NOT IN V1 | Consider only if demanded by regulated customers; would require dedicated hardening |
| S3 / object store archive | No | No | No | N/A | N/A | Not included; retention/archival is a “premium” feature and varies by customer infra | NOT IN V1 | If customer needs archive, recommend exporting from their SIEM/ELK |

* Air‑gapped “Yes” means: supported as long as the sink is reachable on internal network; Redwood ships collector images/configs in the offline bundle. No assumption of cloud-managed Splunk/Elastic endpoints.
** OTLP in air‑gapped installs is typically only workable if the customer runs an in-cluster or in-network OTLP receiver (e.g., OpenTelemetry Collector) that forwards internally; direct-to-vendor SaaS endpoints generally not reachable.

Auth mode details (what we test vs what we’ll accept)
- Splunk HEC
  - Tested: HEC token via "Authorization: Splunk <token>" header
  - TLS: server validation required; allow custom CA via secret
  - Proxy: supported if customer supplies proxy URL and egress rules
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
  - Tested: Basic auth over TLS
  - Documented: API key via header ("Authorization: ApiKey …")
  - Not in v1: AWS SigV4 signing (OpenSearch managed) — requires additional signing support and key handling
- Loki
  - Documented: Basic auth, bearer token
  - Tenant: optional X-Scope-OrgID header if customer uses multi-tenancy
- OTLP HTTP
  - Documented: arbitrary headers (API keys), TLS with custom CA

Operational notes / tuning defaults (minimum pack)
- Buffering
  - Default is memory buffer with bounded size; optional disk buffer for on‑prem with high burstiness (customer must provide PVC).
  - When buffers fill, collector will start dropping (to protect cluster stability). This is called out in runbooks as a deliberate tradeoff.
- Rate limits
  - If sink throttles, we recommend increasing retry backoff and enabling disk buffering rather than increasing concurrency.
- PII/secrets
  - Customers should confirm their sink access controls: logs may contain request_id, route, model, status codes, latency, and error stack traces.
  - Redwood defaults aim to avoid payload logging; customers must not turn on verbose payload logging without a security review.

Customer “ready checklist” (hand to SE/PS)
1) Choose target: Splunk HEC / Elastic/OpenSearch / Loki / OTLP receiver
2) Provide endpoint + DNS + network allow rules
3) Provide auth secret(s) (token or username/password)
4) Provide TLS CA bundle secret (if not publicly trusted)
5) Confirm retention policy on sink side (who owns ILM/retention)
6) If air‑gapped: confirm offline bundle includes collector images + dashboards/rules; confirm no internet dependency for resolving endpoints/certs

Known pitfalls (from support)
- Splunk HEC 401: token invalid, wrong endpoint path, missing "Splunk" prefix in Authorization header
- Empty indices in Elastic: sink reachable but rejected due to index template/mapping or ingest pipeline
- Loki 413 / 502: gateway body size too small for batched pushes
- NetworkPolicy changes: Prometheus/Grafana may be fine but log exporter egress blocked (collector cannot reach sink)

Open questions / next steps
- Decide if we promote Loki from DOCUMENTED → VALIDATED (add to smoke tests) once we have a stable reference Loki chart.
- Revisit SigV4 for OpenSearch if we see repeated enterprise demand (would require secure key handling guidance for private clusters).
- Clarify official stance on disk buffering default for on‑prem (tradeoff: durability vs PVC + ops overhead).

Contact / ownership
- Primary: Colin O'Donnell (customer logging/SIEM constraints)
- Eng owners: Logan Wright (telemetry platform), Diego Santos (private deployments)
- Security review: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei
